clue.text: Shallow versifying in Measure for Measure?

definitions.meaning: Justice Shallow is a Shakespeare character (Henry IV, Merry Wives); if he wrote verse he would be a poetic magistrate
measure for measure means fitting retribution, the deserved comeuppance meted out to wrongdoers

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at the thin verse in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses lean on Shakespeare: one is a character's title and name with a literary adjective, the other the play title read as tit-for-tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution that fits the crime, measure for measure, is the idiom's everyday sense; the first reading jokily makes Justice Shallow a versifier.

clue.text: Eye on a car, perhaps? When do you get your Christmas bonus?

definitions.text: When do you get your Christmas bonus?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of these words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Spotting a car, then wondering about the timing of the annual Christmas bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges EYEONACAR. The definition is a whole question, answered by the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas bonus arrives annually, so the phrase meaning annually answers the question.

clue.text: Time and money absorbed with Queen's fool

indicators.note: absorbed shows time and money soaking up the following letters inside them

parts.note: P, for penny or pence, stands for money
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Time and money are swallowed up by the Queen's jester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' puts W and ER inside T and P together, giving T(WER)P.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insulting synonyms for a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Picasso's model? On the contrary, theirs …

definitions.text: Picasso's model? On the contrary, theirs …

parts.words: Picasso's model? On the contrary, theirs …
parts.note: Picasso suggests the painter and his sitter, but here the French car maker named a people-carrier the Picasso, so Picasso is their model, not the other way round

explanation.surface: A question about who posed for Picasso, turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Xsara Picasso was a car from this French manufacturer, so the model belongs to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The French car maker sold a model called the Picasso, so Picasso is one of its models.

clue.text: Beautiful! An ovation surrounds the Bolshoi's finest!

indicators.note: the clue words surround the answer, which sits within beautiful and ovation

explanation.surface: Applause rings out for a great dancer at the Bolshoi.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'beautifUL AN OVAtion'. Galina Ulanova was the Bolshoi Ballet's prima ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Galina Ulanova was the celebrated prima ballerina assoluta of Moscow's Bolshoi Ballet.

clue.text: Two articles from Anatole France: no French play here!

indicators.note: no French means the abbreviation for French is dropped as well
two articles taken from the novelist's name means they are removed from it

parts.note: the French novelist's name, taken letter by letter
AN and A are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Taking two items from Anatole France leaves no French drama to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AN and A leaves TOLEFRANCE; 'no French' removes F. 'here' is a link; 'play' is the definition, not a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Play in a mechanism is the slack or allowed variation, also called tolerance.

clue.text: On which, quietly speak of pretty girl

indicators.note: speak of tells us to say the letters out loud

parts.note: 'on the QT' means quietly, so QT is the thing on which one acts quietly

explanation.surface: Whispering, on the quiet, about an attractive girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the QT' is an idiom for secretly; the letters QT, spoken, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is informal for an attractive, pretty young woman.

clue.text: Oo! One fruit cake cooked, not a biscuit!

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up and transformed
not a says the letter a is taken out of the mixture

parts.note: the single letter a

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the fruit cake they baked is not a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from OOONEFRUITCAKE ('not a') and rearrange the rest ('cooked').
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp folded cookie, holding a slip of paper, is a type of sweet biscuit.

clue.text: Wow! The libel's fabricated! Right, who blabbed?

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Outrage at a made-up libel, and a demand to know who leaked it.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'libel's' stands for 'libel is', so its S belongs in the anagram; 'fabricated' is the anagram signal, and 'Right' supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exposes wrongdoing by passing secrets on is one who has blabbed.

clue.text: Phil, some say, a royal playing for Liverpool

definitions.meaning: Phil is a common short form of Philharmonic, a name for a symphony ensemble
the Royal Liverpool Philharmonic is the city's famous band of players

explanation.surface: A royal named Phil seems to be turning out for Liverpool football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Prince Philip and football, but the Royal Liverpool Philharmonic is a classical ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A philharmonic is a symphony ensemble, and the Royal Liverpool Philharmonic is one.

clue.text: Rut cut in from left

indicators.note: in from left means the letter for left comes in at the left-hand end

parts.note: to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: A rut is cut into the ground from the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in from' places L at the front of ETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Letch means lustful craving, and rut is an animal's sexual heat, so both are lust.

clue.text: Broad, conclusively representative art retrospective

indicators.note: conclusively puts the representative at the end of the answer
retrospective means looking back, so the word art is read backwards

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A broad retrospective exhibition of representative art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns ART into TRA; 'conclusively' puts MP last. Broad is old US slang for a woman, here a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad and tramp are both dated, derogatory American slang for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: With no trace of Les Miserables, singularly leading in the British charts

indicators.note: in places the miserable Les inside the British maps

parts.note: OS, the Ordnance Survey, makes Britain's official maps

indicators.note: leading puts the gloomy word ahead of the name

parts.note: taken in the singular, miserable means dour
the French word taken as written

explanation.surface: Les Miserables has gone from the British charts without a trace, though it once led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' orders the gloomy word before the name, and 'in' sets both inside the maps; 'of' is a link. Les Misérables is a long-running London musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odourless leaves no trace of smell, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Miserable Les; no German holds with backing this composer

indicators.note: holds means the backward German word contains the shuffled name
backing means the German word is read in reverse

parts.note: nein is German for no

indicators.note: miserable suggests the name Les is in a poor state and jumbled

explanation.surface: Miserable Les says no in German, holding out for this composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserable' rearranges LES to LSE; 'backing' turns NEIN to NIEN, which 'holds' LSE. 'with' is a link. Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: Hill's thorn-bound 7am delivery service?

parts.note: Rowland Hill founded the penny post; Browning's Pippa Passes has morning at seven and the snail on the thorn, so a slow creature brings the post

explanation.surface: A question about an early-morning delivery service.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowland Hill created Britain's penny post. Browning's Pippa's Song: 'Morning's at seven ... The snail's on the thorn'. The answer is jocular for slow conventional post.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is joking slang for ordinary postal delivery, slow compared with email.

clue.text: Last Stuart detailed first victim; Ms Lee?

indicators.note: detailed means having its tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Queen Anne was the last Stuart monarch
Abel, killed by Cain, was the first murder victim in the Bible

explanation.surface: The final Stuart is dismembered as the first victim of someone called Ms Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the E from ANNE. Annabel Lee is the subject of Edgar Allan Poe's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's poem 'Annabel Lee' names a woman with the surname Lee, so she is a Ms Lee.

clue.text: Without ceremony, brother, I've returned Old Trafford's shorts!

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back the other way

parts.note: the contraction taken as its letters
Man U is the short name of Manchester United, whose ground is Old Trafford

explanation.surface: My brother casually brought back his Manchester United football shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IVE into EVI. Old Trafford is Manchester United's football ground; 'shorts' signals short forms, not kit.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, literally 'with a short hand', means summarily, without formality.

clue.text: French horn's theme in Berlioz's overture

parts.note: cor is French for horn, plus the possessive s
an air is a tune or melodic theme

explanation.surface: The French horn plays the main theme in an overture by Berlioz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'French horn' reads as the instrument but means horn in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Corsaire is a concert overture by Hector Berlioz.

clue.text: Trout knocked off by Lawrence?

definitions.meaning: a familiar freshwater game fish species takes this name
knocked off means written quickly; D. H. Lawrence wrote a novel of this title

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fish was killed by a man called Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked off' suggests killing, but means dashed off as writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a species, and The Rainbow is a 1915 novel by D. H. Lawrence.

clue.text: Non-Reithian reference to his fiefdom?

parts.note: Lord Reith, first head of the British Broadcasting Corporation, insisted on formality; an informal nickname for his domain would be un-Reithian

explanation.surface: A question about an informal name for a lord's domain.
explanation.walkthrough: John Reith founded the BBC's public-service ethos; the casual nickname for the corporation is the opposite of his style.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the affectionate informal British nickname for the BBC, Reith's corporation.

clue.text: Hot nudist refreshed with a funnel

indicators.note: refreshed means renewed, so these letters are made over in a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A hot nudist cools off with the help of a funnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshed' rearranges H and NUDIST. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tundish is a funnel-shaped vessel, used in plumbing and in steel casting.

clue.text: Authoritarian, dehumanising and oppressive: like Blair?

definitions.meaning: describes the totalitarian state imagined in Nineteen Eighty-Four
Eric Blair was the real name of the author of Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: A complaint that a regime is oppressive, like Tony Blair's.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair suggests the Prime Minister Tony Blair, but means Eric Blair, the novelist's real name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes oppressive surveillance states as in Nineteen Eighty-Four, and also anything like its author, Eric Blair.

clue.text: Fish so called with a new lawyer in New York

parts.note: a DA, district attorney, is an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A fish is named after a new lawyer in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The film 'A Fish Called Wanda' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film A Fish Called Wanda the title fish bears this name.

clue.text: Who's the would-be geisha around here? All right! I am!

indicators.note: around means the whole phrase is turned to read the other way

parts.note: OK means all right
the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks who the trainee geisha is, and a voice replies that it is she.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns OKIAM backwards. 'Who's the' and 'here' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiko is an apprentice geisha in Kyoto, still training for the role.

clue.text: Impulsive transmitter of verse between masses

indicators.note: between places the verse inside the two masses

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass, so masses gives two Ms
an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A passionate broadcaster of poetry among the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. 'Impulsive' means sending electrical impulses, not acting rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem transmits data as electrical pulses down a line, so it sends impulses.

clue.text: Holy Island welcoming one Greek outpost

indicators.note: welcoming means the island takes the letter in

parts.note: Iona is the Scottish island where St Columba founded his monastery
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sacred island welcomes a single Greek visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a Hebridean island off western Scotland, sacred for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the ancient Greek colony region on the coast of Asia Minor.

clue.text: Love at first sight sought on this appointment?

definitions.text: Love at first sight sought on this appointment?

parts.words: Love at first sight sought on this appointment?
parts.note: a meeting arranged between people who have never seen each other, where the hope is instant attraction

explanation.surface: A question about where people hope to fall in love at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first sight' is literal: the pair see each other for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranged meeting with an unseen stranger is literally where love at first sight might strike.

clue.text: Topping gag inducing low, glum, sour 'Ha!'

indicators.note: inducing suggests the words bring about a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A great joke that produces a gloomy, sour laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inducing' rearranges LOWGLUMSOURHA. 'Topping' means excellent on the surface but hanging in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is slang for hanging, so a gag about execution is grim comedy of this kind.
